newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian gypsies poisoned by horse meat - police.
newsitem.headline: Romanian gypsies poisoned by horse meat - police.

text.p: More than 60 Gypsies from a village in northwest Romania were in hospital with food poisoning after eating horse meat, police said on Monday.

Police in Oradea, on the border with Hungary, said 64 members of a Gypsy community reported food poisoning symptoms after eating meat from a three-month-old foal which a Gypsy leader had bought on the cheap from a horse trader.

Food poisoning is common in post-communist Romania, where at least 13 people have died this year from poisonous mushrooms. The latest four deaths, including two children, were reported last week, after floods affected the Balkan country.

Many poverty-stricken Romanians resort to eating cheap meat bought from shady peddlars or ignore a ban on unauthorised picking and sales of mushrooms. More than 60 people, mostly children, have suffered from eating poisoned mushrooms.
